about: Every dimension the F/A-18C build uses, with its source (an id in references.json) and where in it. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts. Stations (FS) are inches aft of the fuselage datum, waterlines (WL) inches above it (WL 100 is the fuselage reference line), buttlines (BL) inches from the centreline, positive to starboard. Angles round the fuselage (theta) follow TM-101724 figure 3: looking aft, 0 is the bottom centreline, 180 the top, 90 starboard and 270 port. A fact taken from the old model, as a last resort, names the old model as its source and says why no other source had it; a detail copied from it under the fair-use policy is listed in its manifest entry (air-fa18c.md #2).

length.also: hatp figure 2 (56.00 ft); tp209033 figure 2 (56.0 ft)
length.note: checked to the foot NATOPS gives it in (+-6 in; user, 2026-11-02): with the stabilator tips' 13 in corner rounds where the photos put them (layout.stabilator, layout.stabilator_corner) the model measures 55.76 ft, and the photos' own apex (FS 59.7, 18 photos) and aftmost point (FS 729.8) give 55.84 ft

exhaust.note: nose apex to the engine exhaust plane: the nozzles' exit (layout.nozzle)
exhaust.also: tp3478 PDF page 6 (54.4 ft, nose to exhaust nozzle exit plane, full scale)

spread.note: 37 ft 6 in, without missiles. hatp figure 2 gives the reference span as 37.417 ft

fins.note: 15 ft 3 in, to the top of the fins
fins.also: tp209033 figure 2 (15.3 ft, on its gear)

canopy.note: 10 ft 6 in, to the top of the closed canopy

gravity.note: moment reference at 25% of the mean aerodynamic chord

station.note: moment reference at 25% of the mean aerodynamic chord, WL 100.00, BL 0

leading.note: leading edge of the mean aerodynamic chord (11.52 ft)

apex.also: tp209033 figure 2 (FS 59.82); tm110216 figure 3.1 (FS 59.9); tp3111 figure 7 (FS 60.60)

droop.note: the nosecone centreline is depressed 5.6 deg; the first three stations are canted forward to match

sections.note: from the LEX-fuselage junction to the LEX leading edge

graph.note: LEX local span on the full-scale jet, read off the graph to about 1 in; runs about 1 in above tm101724's three stations

fence.unit: in, FS in, BL in, deg
fence.where: figure 7, PDF page 33; text PDF page 8
fence.note: the 0.06-scale model's fence, in full-scale inches: normal to the LEX surface at its leading edge, about 25 deg from vertical

hardware.note: the full-scale fence fitted to fleet jets; its lengths differ from tp3111's model fence, so the 2020s photos settle the shape

gun.note: the gun port exits, on the upper centreline near FS 122

probe.note: the in-flight refuelling probe doors, upper starboard side

pitot.note: the two production pitot-static probes, lower fuselage

ecm.note: two elliptical ECM antenna covers on the research jet; confirm on the 2020s reference airframe

scale.note: the 0.06-scale wind-tunnel model's three-view: b = 2.245 ft, length 3.360 ft, S = 1.44 ft2, mean chord 0.691 ft

surfaces.about: Surface positions NATOPS gives for each flap setting, in degrees down, and the mechanical limits (limits).

ground.note: HALF or FULL on the ground; AUTO with weight on wheels is 0

fixed.note: GAIN ORIDE with HALF or FULL

check.where: ground checklist, spin recovery mode check
check.note: 33 +/- 1 deg down with the spin recovery mode engaged: the most the flaps travel in NATOPS

differential.note: up to +/-3 deg below 30,000 ft above Mach 0.7

half.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

full.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

trim.note: takeoff trim drives the stabilator to 12 deg nose up

limits.about: Mechanical position and rate limits, deg and deg/s, from tp209033 table 2 (PDF page 16), which states they are the basic F-18A/B's. tm110216 table 6.2 (PDF page 99) gives the HARV's aileron as 25 up and 42 down.

waterline.note: the fuselage reference line corresponds to WL 100.0 on the airplane

buttline.note: BL 0 is the centreline; BL grows to starboard (Y is right of the c.g.)

apex.note: the fuselage reference line (WL 100) is drawn through the nose apex and on aft past the stabilator; tp209033 figure 2 points WL 100 at the stabilator

chord.note: mean aerodynamic chord, projected; tp209033 and hatp give 11.52 ft (138.24 in) as the reference chord

root.note: NACA 65A with a sharp leading edge, at wing station 56.876 (cr201687 table 1: modified NACA 65A, 5.0%)

tip.note: cr201687 table 1 agrees (3.5%); secondary sources' 65A003 is not supported

span.note: span station of the wingtip at the launcher rail, on a sketch; the reference semispan is 224.5 in

lef.note: each inboard leading-edge flap is 36.5% of the total LEF area, each outboard 13.5%; one actuator drives both

areas.note: totals for both sides. cr3608's 1/10-scale model gives 0.19, 0.55 and 0.62 ft2, which scale to 19, 55 and 62. The flaps' 48.4 is not built: their fronts stand on the hinge line the photos show (layout.hinge), which makes them 55.5

exposed.note: reference span of the exposed panels

area.note: theoretical exposed, both sides; tm4772 table 1 gives 88.26 unmodified

toe.note: toe out, as the model table gives it

top.note: the fin tip 11.34 in above the fuselage reference line on the 1/10-scale model. Anchored at the apex, the HATP side view draws it about 4 in higher and its canopy top at WL 163, which this figure also draws

forebody.note: the McDonnell Douglas drawing's forebody height and width, read off the graphs to about 1 in; agrees with tm101724's sections

buttline.note: TLOC: each engine axis 2.33 ft either side of the centreline at the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56), where the figure draws it

angle.note: EPS: the engine axis's angle to the aircraft's x axis in plan. The axes converge aft: hatp figure 2's top view draws the nozzles at BL 19.5 either side, nearly touching, as photo dvids9820758 shows, which 2 deg of convergence from 28 in at FS 458.56 gives (19.3 in at FS 707)

thrust.note: DXTHRS: the thrust point's distance aft of the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56)

inlet.note: hydraulic diameter of the inlet duct entrance

canopy.note: how much bigger the two-seat canopy is than the single-seat one; tp209033 figure 2 draws the two-seat jet

gravity.aircraft: HARV phase 1, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
HARV phases 2-3, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
F-18B SRA, 66% fuel, clean, gear up

airfoils.note: NACA 65A basic thickness forms: half-thickness y at chordwise station x, both in percent of chord. Another thickness takes y/t interpolated linearly in t between the tabulated forms (TR-84's own method, by its cross plots); above 5% the 5% ratios hold, which TR-84's 63-series cross plots show moving under 2% between 5% and 6%.

layout.about: Placements no source states, fitted to the NASA three-views with the published planforms (views.py's masks, the side view anchored at the apex on WL 100). Each says what it was fitted to. Provisional until the reference airframe's photos confirm them.

wing.where: figure 5, PDF page 31 (traced by views.py), with hatp figure 2's side view for the keel. The anhedral: photos.py's cameras and tips.py (rotating the wing about the junction; deflections fitted, or held at rest in flight) over the ground photo dvids9820799 and the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145, their cameras solved with the rest (fin tips within 0.3 in)
wing.note: the wing's chord plane at the LEX-wing junction (BL 54.5, FS 404.05): the FS 357 section's LEX tip stands 31 in above its keel, and the keel is at WL 82.5. The anhedral is the photos', the jet parked (the user's choice, 2026-10-30): cr201687's -3 deg (wing.dihedral) leaves the tips' trailing corners about 5 in low in the ground photo (+-2 in or more: its flaps and ailerons droop) and 10 in low in three in-flight photos (8.7-10.3 leaving each out), the difference the wing bending up at 1 g (task: wing flex). Rotating the wing about the junction fits the flight photos a little better than raising it, and the junction itself measures no higher (4 in lower, +-2.3, two photos). The HATP front view draws the outer wing about 10 in higher

flex.unit: BL in, where the bend starts; in, the wingtip's rise at 1 g of lift; [BL in, share of the tip's rise]
flex.where: the rise: tm212871 printed page 17 and figure 12(a), FDMS target 12 (span station 193.8, figure 5) about 1.4 in, and 1.7 in after a roll, in steady level flight against ground rest, taken to the tip by the ground test's shape; the shape: tm210726 figure 16, load case D3, the forward box's measured deflection (1.1, 1.8, 3.1, 5.1, 6.2 and 10.0 in at the stations, 13.6 in at span station 222.1), read off the figure
flex.note: the wing bent up by lift (task: wing flex), as the shape key flex and the bend joints flex_* driven by the load factor of the lift (the drive load: 0 parked, 1 in level flight). Both reports fly the Active Aeroelastic Wing jet, whose wing has the preproduction torsional stiffness, a little softer than a production C's; its targets outboard of the fold carry the fold's free play. The bend starts at the LEX-wing junction (layout.wing's buttline) and takes a cantilever's shape, lift along the span as the chord and stiffness as the chord times the section's depth squared, streamwise sections rigid: outboard of BL 150 it follows the ground test's shape within 0.015 of the tip's rise, inboard it bends 0.05-0.06 less (the test's load and the fuselage's restraint are not flight's). The photo match agrees within its uncertainty: posed at 1 g with the in-flight photos, the wingtips' trailing corners fit best near a 3.5 in rise and the parked photos' wing and fin edges best with none

stabilator.where: figure 2, top view; natops 1.1.2 for the length; the waterline from the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145 (tips.py, deflections held at rest, the cameras photos.py solved)
stabilator.note: the root leading edge of the exposed panel (BL 41.6: the 21.6 ft span less the 14.67 ft exposed span). The views from straight above and below (dvids7487365, 7487366, 9820744), each photo's left and right sides averaged to cancel its camera's registration, read the leading edge 0.1 in and the trailing edge 0.05 in from the model's here (sky check); moving the panel 1.8 or 2.9 in aft took them to -0.6 and +1.5, or -0.9 and +2.5. It was first placed for the 56 ft overall length with an 8 in corner round; with the photos' 13 in round (layout.stabilator_corner) the tips' aftmost point falls at FS 729.8, 2.9 in short of it, and the photos' own apex and aftmost point give 55.84 ft (overall.length). WL 106.8: the in-flight photos put the tips' leading corners 6.8 in above where cr3608 figure 3's and tp209033 figure 2's WL 100 had them (6.3-7.7 leaving each photo out; 4-7.5 with trim free), the root then 3.8 in above the engine axes (layout.nozzle, WL 103); the HATP side view draws them about 10 in higher. The spindle is not published

stabilator_corner.where: the sky check's photo edge places round each stabilator's trailing tip corner, cast onto the posed panel's plane, fitted as the cited tip line and trailing edge joined by a circle tangent to both, the panel's offset free (each photo's registration): 13.25 and 13.25 in (dvids7487365 left and right), 12.0 and 12.25 (dvids9820744), 13.0 and 13.0 (dvids7487366), 12.25 (dvids7487368 right), fitting to 0.13-0.19 in rms (0.52 for the last). The model's own outline through the same fit reads 7.5-8.0 for its 8. Variants with the panel unmoved: the corner's sky check, each photo's sides averaged, read +2.76 in with 8 in and +0.51 with 13 in, the leading and trailing edges unchanged (+0.10, +0.05). HATP figure 2's top view, a small drawing, cuts the corner back about 11 in along the tip, where a 13 in round leaves the tip line visibly (by 0.5 in) about 17 in from the corner
stabilator_corner.note: the radius of the round on each stabilator tip's trailing corner, tangent to the tip and to the trailing edge, 20.5 in from the corner along each; it takes 1.3 ft2 off the 88.0 for both sides (stabilator.area). cr201687's planform, which the build keeps everywhere else, is the theoretical one with sharp corners. Judged by where the traced tip seemed to leave its line it was first put at 8 in: a 13 in circle stays within 0.5 in of its tangent for 3.6 in past the tangent point. The leading corner reads sharp and the leading edge straight within a few degrees of the cited sweep. The corner landmarks stay where the edges' lines meet, as the photos are marked

fin.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): the fin tips' four corners in 6-9 photos (+-1.8 in along, +-0.3 in across); moved 1.5 in forward (2026-10-31): the fin tips' leading corners in 15-16 photos stand 2.0 in forward of the earlier build (+-2.2) and the trailing corners 2.9 in (+-2.4), and the sky check (verify/skyline.py) reads the leading edge 0.6-1.0 in inside the photos' all along it (FS 528-624, 10-14 photos each), about 1.0 in of stations at its sweep: the move lies between the two; moved 1.0 in further forward (2026-11-02): the tips' leading corners in 16-17 photos stood 1.0 in forward of the build (+-1.3) and the trailing corners 2.0 in (+-1.4), the leading edges traced in 13 photos and cast onto each fin's own plane 1.2 in forward all along their height on both fins (no sweep the photos agree on: single photos tilt both ways), and the sky check read the leading edge 0.4 in inside and the aft end 1.0 in outside
fin.note: leading edge at root and tip, on cr201687's planform, sweep and cant: the photos put the tips 8 in further aft and 7 in further outboard than the HATP views were fitted to give (FS 613.6, BL 71.4), the HATP side view's own top trailing corner standing 8.8 in aft of the old fit too; the root lies 95 in down the 20 deg cant from the tip (BL 38.9, on the nacelle's shoulder)

hinge.where: dvids7487365 (straight below, sharp, against clear sky): one straight line, with the hinge fittings and actuator fairings on it, runs along the lower surface of both wings across the flap and the aileron; traced at 16 points (BL 57-225 right, 57-211 left), cast onto the posed wing, it lies at 0.704-0.720 of the chord, rising inboard; the value is the median of the 11 points along the flaps. The aileron's front, which cr201687's aileron area sets (wing.areas, 0.699), stands 0.3-1.0 in ahead of it on both wings; cr201687's flap area would have put the flap's front 4.6-5.0 in behind it
hinge.note: the lower surface's hinge line of the trailing-edge flap and the aileron, as a share of the wing's chord from the leading edge. The flaps' fronts are built on it, which makes them 55.5 ft2 for both sides, where cr201687 table 1 gives 48.4 and cr3608's 1/10-scale model 62; the flaps' area is not built. The traced line is a photo match edge (dvids7487365 hinge_*), which the old flap missed by 4.3-4.4 in. dvids9820744, softer, read the same line 1.2-5.0 in ahead of the old flap front and 3.1-4.2 in behind the aileron's: both now about 3 in off it the same way, its camera's registration

surfaces.unit: BL in; the rudder as fractions of the fin's span from its root
surfaces.where: figure 2 (control surfaces labelled in the top and side views); the flap's outer end and the aileron's inner end by photo match, with tm210726 figure 6
surfaces.note: spans of the hinged surfaces: the leading-edge flaps split at the fold (tp209033 PDF page 17) and run from the LEX-wing junction to the tip; the flap's inner end and the rudder's are read off figure 2's sketch. The flap's outer trailing corner is the photo match's fold_trailing point (BL 152.8 +- 0.8, six marks in five photos), 7 in inboard of the sketch's 160; the gap to the aileron is 3.1 in wide at the trailing edge in dvids9820744. tm210726 figure 6 (to scale within 1%: its two references and the tip agree) draws the load zones on the flap ending at BL 154 and those on the aileron starting at 156. The aileron's inboard 6.5 in lies behind the fold line and folds with the outer panel. The aileron runs to the tip (the sketch drew it ending at BL 220): with it drooped in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788, sky shows directly outboard of its end, under the tip's launcher rail. Each surface's chord fraction follows from its cr201687 area over these spans

gear.unit: FS in for the axle centres; WL in for the axles; in for the track (between the main wheels' centres) and the nose wheels' spacing
gear.where: NATOPS 1.1.2's heights for the axles; verify/photos.py over photos.json for the track and the nose wheels' spacing (the wheels' hub faces in 6-9 photos, +-0.4 in across); tp209033 figure 2 for the stations, which the photos confirm (FS 495.1 and 280.9, +-1.2)
gear.note: the wheel centres' stations from the nose apex on tp209033 figure 2 (FS 59.82 marked) at its 56 ft scale, wheelbase 17.77 ft. The axles' heights are set so NATOPS's static heights hold over the ground beneath the tyres (fins 15 ft 3 in, canopy 10 ft 6 in): the jet then sits 0.9 deg nose down. The photos' taxiing jets put the main axle 2.9 in higher (WL 44.3 +-1.5) and the nose axle 0.8 in higher (45.6 +-0.9), more nose down, as a lighter or moving jet may sit. The track is the photos': the main hub faces stand 66.2 in either side, less a third of each tyre's width to its centre (tp209033's rear view drew the track 116 in). The nose wheels' spacing is dvids8559777's, head-on: both tyres cast onto the axle's station plane from its solved camera stand at BL +8.6 and -8.2, each 6.4-6.5 in wide against the 6.6 in read off the close-ups, so the cast's scale holds; a steered pair would read narrower, not wider. The photo match agrees within its spread (the hub faces at BL 10.3-11.3, about 2 in further out than the 8.9 an earlier solve gave, when one photo's mark on a far wheel's inboard face pulled its camera to 16 px). Tyre diameters from dvids9820808's matched camera; widths read off the gear close-ups dvids8678626 and dvids8678628 against those diameters

canopy.unit: FS in, WL in; the sill as [FS, WL, BL]; top, the canopy's top line behind the crown as [FS, WL]; glass, the exponents of the superellipse the glass's section follows from the sill to the top centreline, at the bow's foot and at the aft corner (linear between); screen, the windscreen's frame sill as [FS, WL, BL] ahead of the bow's foot; screen_glass, [FS, exponent]: the windscreen glass's superellipse exponent, held to that station and rising linearly to glass's first at the bow's foot; joint, [FS, WL, BL] along the joint where the canopy's aft fairing meets the spine, from its top down to the sill; glass_edge, [FS, WL] readings along the glass's lower edge on the left, where the metal panel below it meets it
canopy.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): windscreen_base in 5 photos, bow_top 2, canopy_aft 3, bow_foot 4, sill_aft 4 (+-1 in); canopy_crown and the sill's middle in dvids9820808 alone. The sill's buttlines from the 22-photo solve (2026-11-02): bow_foot BL 15.24 in 8 photos and sill_aft 20.15 in 7 (+-0.4), each 1.3-1.6 in further out than the first solve put them, which every single photo left out keeps (1.06-1.81); the middle, which only dvids9820808 sees, moved out by their mean. TM 101724's cited sections (FS 184-253) agree: they stand 2-2.5 in wider than the earlier sill. glass and top: the canopy outlines traced in the seven photos with well-solved cameras, split fore and aft by the station of the model's silhouette nearest each traced point, the cameras held while only the canopy changes. The glass's upper edge against the sky in the profiles dvids9820808 and dvids9820801 (the strongest step in each pixel column, cast onto the centreline) gives the top line behind the crown; the two agree within 0.15 in (0.45 at FS 264), three readings that caught the cockpit inside left out. With that top line the outlines' median miss is 0.28 in (1.00 with the cited sections unchanged): forward of FS 280 any exponent from 1.8 to 2.3 does as well, aft 1.0 and 1.2 do (0.20 and 0.25 in) while 1.6 and 2.0 miss by 0.55 and 0.83 screen: the windscreen frame's sill line traced in the side photos (layout.panels, sill_line_right), sampled. screen_glass (2026-11-02): with the windscreen's section above it drawn in to a superellipse, the quarter views' sky outline just behind the front base (FS 192-216, BL 8-13) read +1.18 in with an exponent of 2.0, +1.25 with 1.6, +0.69 with 1.3 and +0.47 with 1.1 (where the head-up display's glass then pokes through); 1.3 held back to the bow drew the glass at FS 216-240 0.77 in inside, so it rises to the canopy's 2.0 at the bow's foot from FS 200: +0.82 there over 7 photos (was +1.22), the glass at FS 216-240 -0.01 over 9, dvids9820748's traced windscreen edge 0.19 in (was 1.04) joint (2026-11-03): the seam behind the canopy's aft fairing traced in dvids9820801 (right) and triangulated against its mirror image traced in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788 (left): the two left photos agree within 0.3 in, each pixel 0.0-0.4 px off the traced line; the point at the top (BL 11.3) missed by 3-6 px and is left out. Cast onto the skin instead, the right photo put the joint at FS 333-334 and the left at 338-339 over a spine faded too long behind the canopy (2 in low there) glass_edge (2026-11-04): the glass's lower edge, its dark seal line found column by column in dvids9820782 (FS 254-317) and dvids9820788 (FS 280-315) and cast onto the canopy's skin: the two agree within 0.5 in where both see it. It runs 3.5 in above the sill at FS 254 and rises steadily to WL 151.5 at FS 317, a broad metal panel below it, ahead of the canopy's aft end
canopy.note: the windscreen's front base, the bow between windscreen and canopy, the canopy's crown and aft end on the centreline, and the canopy's sill from the bow's foot to the canopy's aft lower corner. The cited sections between FS 184 and 253 leave the skin 2-2.5 in wider than the sill, so the build draws the glass in to meet it

eye.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json: dvids9820808's helmet located from its camera solved with the other 11 photos, centre FS 254.5 WL 154.4, top WL 159.3
eye.note: the design eye, provisional: a little ahead of and below the helmet's centre in the reference photo, where the pilot sits reaching for the canopy bow

hardpoints.where: figure 4-4 (External Stores Limitations): each station's distance from the centreline, 19.5 ft (stations 1 and 9), 11.2 (2 and 8), 7.3 (3 and 7) and 3.7 (4 and 6), to a tenth of a foot
hardpoints.note: stations 1-9 (air-stores.md). A station's buttline is the figure's distance, where its store hangs. The wing stations' mounts sit on the wing's lower surface at that buttline and the chord fraction given, the store straight below; the tip stations' on the wingtip (the build places them there, not at the buttline), whose launcher carries the round out to the figure's line; the fuselage stations' on the skin straight below their station and buttline, the cheek stations' inboard of their rounds (station 6). The stations along the length and the chord fraction are provisional until step 5 matches the stores themselves. The flight model's store positions (fa18c.go) are its own estimates, not this figure: its outboard pylons at 3.35 m (131.9 in) and its cheek stations at 0.55 m (21.7 in), 'a plausible figure, not a survey'. The photos' Litening pod hangs on the centreline at FS 350-445 (dvids7487365, dvids9820744 and dvids8901347 agree), forward of station 5: its adapter, not the station, places it

stations.where: NATOPS figure 4-4 hangs the round 3.7 ft (44.4 in) out, and dvids7487365 (from below) agrees: its right-cheek AIM-120's nose and tail, cast from the solved camera, put the axis at FS 420-567 (the round's 144 in) and BL 46.8 at WL 70, less 0.24 in for each inch higher, so BL 44.4 at WL 80. The round's inboard side clears the nacelle (BL 38.2 at WL 80, 42.4 at WL 84, at FS 496) only below WL 82, so it hangs against the nacelle's lower outboard corner with its axis about WL 80. The mount is the skin straight above its inboard side, BL 41.5, which the build drapes to WL 85.8; the station is the round's middle

lights.where: 2.6.1 (position, formation, strobe, approach, landing, hook and probe lights)
lights.note: what the jet carries and roughly where; every position here is provisional until the reference photos are matched, the position lights after the engine's own (LEX edge ahead of the wing root, under the wing at the fold)

lex.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json: lex_apex in 7 photos (+-0.8 in), 12 photos solved together; the fence's top corners in 8 photos (+-1.6 in across, 2.0 in in height), 21 solved together
lex.note: where the LEX's edge leaves the body, 7 in aft of and 5 in below where cr186938's graph extrapolates it (FS 189); and the top corners of the fleet LEX fence, which stands on tp3111's base (lex.fence: FS 378.17 to 410.33 at BL 42)

probe.unit: FS in; degrees from the top centreline
probe.where: the door's lower corners cast onto the skin: each solved camera's sight line through probe_door_front (dvids9820810, dvids9820801) and probe_door_aft (dvids9820808, dvids9820810, dvids9820801) meets the fuselage at WL 123.3-123.7 and 131.4-131.8 (38 and 36 deg round), FS 144.2-145.6 and 185.8-189.1. The upper edge: tm101724's (fittings.probe), theta 165 from the keel
probe.note: the reference airframe's probe door, shorter than the research jet's (fittings.probe, FS 128.5 to 188). The photos are all right-side views, so the bundle alone leaves the corners 3-4 in inside the skin along their sight lines; the skin fixes that depth. The upper edge is the research jet's, 15 deg round from the top: one solved photo sees it, dvids9820799 at a grazing 16 deg, casting it at BL 7.0-8.7 (and the lower edge at 11.5-13, against the corners' 12.2-14.4 on the skin), which so flat a view leaves uncertain by inches. An unsolved photo looking down on another jet (dvids3435192) agrees: it reads the edge 12-14 deg round, parallel to the centreline (BL 4.7-5.1 by its own calibration, which puts the lower edge 2-3 in inboard of the skin-cast one; scaled to that, BL 6.0-6.5 against the built 5.3-6.2); that jet's lower edge, 42 deg round, lies 5 deg below the photos'

aoa.unit: FS, WL in; the base plate's diameter, the cone's length and base diameter in
aoa.where: cast onto the skin: the right probe seen end-on in dvids9820808 (FS 164.4, WL 103.3), the left probe's base in dvids9820782 (FS 163.6, WL 103.8); its size read in dvids8678631 at 0.11 in per pixel, where the cone stands across the line of sight
aoa.note: the two angle-of-attack probes (natops 2.19.1), a cone standing straight out of each side of the nose on a round plate; both photos' projections land on the probes in dvids8678631 and dvids9820799

pitot.unit: FS, WL in; the tube's buttline in; the tube's diameter in
pitot.where: dvids9820808: the strut's root cast onto the skin (BL 13.1), its bend and the tube's tip onto the root's buttline; the left tube in dvids9820782 and both in dvids9820799 lie where these project; the tubes' buttline from the two views from below: both tips cast onto their WL from the solved cameras stand 15.1 in (dvids7487365, nearly straight below) and 15.3 in (navy090707N7665E003) either side of the centreline, and the photo match measures 14.95 (+-0.38, 7 marks)
pitot.note: the two pitot-static tubes under the nose (natops 2.12.1): a strut swept forward and down from the skin, canted outboard from its root on the skin (BL 13.1) to the tube, the tube pointing forward from its foot. tm101724's FS 164 to 177 (fittings.pitot) agrees within 0.3 in

blisters.unit: [from FS, to FS, WL at the middle, width round the section, standing proud] in
blisters.where: ends and edges cast onto the skin: dvids9820808 (right) and dvids9820782 (left), which agree within 1 in of station and 2 in of waterline
blisters.note: antenna fairings on each side of the nose, above the formation light strip and on the gun bay's door; how far each stands proud is not measured, but taken in the ECM cover's proportion (fittings.ecm: 1.7 in on a 4 in width). The ECM covers are built from fittings.ecm, which the photos match (FS 128.2 to 137.5, centre WL 106.0, against tm101724's 129.3 to 138.8 and WL 105.7)

formation.where: the forward strip's ends and edges cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 (right) and dvids9820782 (left), which agree within 0.6 in
formation.note: the electroluminescent formation light strips on each side of the nose (natops 2.6.1), flush with the skin

paint.unit: sRGB, 0-255; turn: the range of the surface normal's upward component over which the upper grey gives way to the lower; nozzle: the bare metal of the outer flaps, the divergent flaps' faces inside, and the convergent flaps, the duct beyond the throat and the dark ring of brackets at the exit; holes: the divergent flaps' cooling holes, columns and rows a flap and their radius in inches
paint.where: dvids9820808, overcast: the mean of a clean patch of the fin's side (upper; 80 x 60 px at 1400-1480, 2350-2400, spread 3) and of the nose gear door's downward face (lower; 100 x 40 px at 5300-5400, 3080-3120, spread 5)
paint.note: the nozzles' colours are chosen by eye against the reference jet's parked nozzles (dvids9820749, dvids9820808) and the open nozzles of usaf120811FON144293 and navy020214N3896H001, not measured: the reference jet's nozzles stand in shadow in every photo (sRGB 9-80), and the open-nozzle photos are sunlit or lit by flash. The tactical greys, expected FS 36320 over 36375 (plan #8). The photo's light is in them: the lower grey faces away from the overcast sky and still reads 1.24 times as bright. The fins, whose outer faces tilt 20 deg down with their cant, keep the upper grey; the turn starts just below that

panels.unit: rings: stations of joints round the fuselage; lines: polylines of [FS, WL, BL] on the skin (mirrored ones are copied to the other side); width in; shade, the paint's brightness on a line
panels.where: the radome's joint cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 (FS 127.9 to 128.1, top and bottom); tm101724's nose.junction gives 128.5. The lines, in order: fuselage_side_lower_right (mirrored), door_edge_359_right (mirrored), door_edge_327_right (mirrored), door_edge_287_right (mirrored), door_edge_234_right (mirrored), panel_edge_204_right, panel_edge_204_left_lower, panel_lower_234_204_right (mirrored), door_hinge_right (mirrored), latch_panel_right, access_panel_195_right, access_panel_175_right, access_door_left, sill_line_right (mirrored), spine_side_right (mirrored), spine_joint_335, spine_joint_385, spine_joint_422, spine_joint_456, spine_joint_491, spine_joint_521, fin_root_panel_right, fin_root_panel_left, fin_root_fillet_right (mirrored), nacelle_side_right (mirrored), afterbody_joint_right (mirrored): traced in dvids9820801, 9820808, 9820810, 9820782 and 9820788 and cast onto the skin (verify/cast.py), each checked in a second photo where one shows it (most within 0.1-1.3 in)
panels.note: the panel lines baked into the paint, 0.4 in wide: under one texel of the 2048 atlas (0.47 in), so each texel takes the share of it a line covers (wholly on or off by its centre, they broke into dots). The mirrored lines were traced on the right and copied to the left; one oblique left photo (9820782) puts the doors' edges at FS 234, 287 and 327 1-2.5 in further forward, unsettled. The spine joints' tops (10-12 in either side of the centreline) no photo sees: filled along the skin at the same station. The spine lines were cast from dvids9820801, which sees them nearly abeam: the model's spine aft of FS 440 is broader than the photos' (a task), so they need casting again when it changes. Single-photo: panel_edge_204_left_lower, spine_joint_385, fin_root_panel_left, nacelle_side_right, afterbody_joint_right. nacelle_side_right and afterbody_joint_right were cast again onto the lowered underside behind FS 540 (2026-10-31): the afterbody joint now runs round the boat-tail at FS 660.4-661.2, where on the old skin it slanted 664 to 668 spine_joint_335 (2026-11-03) is the joint behind the canopy's aft fairing, triangulated (layout.canopy joint), its top filled along the skin at FS 334.4: cast before, it lay 1.5 in aft of where two photos either side put it. spine_side_right ahead of FS 404 (2026-11-03) is the seam triangulated from both sides (layout.spine side), from the joint's foot. Lines 6, 7 and 22 re-laid onto the skin at FS 312-415 (2026-11-04), where the fuselage behind the canopy took the old model's section (layout.dorsal): each point moved across onto it, outboard on the sides, down onto the top

stencils.unit: at: [FS, WL] of the stencil's middle on each side's skin; size: [length along the stations, height] in; dark and light: the paint's brightness under the stencil's ink and its lettering
stencils.where: corners cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 (right): the warning box FS 299.4-319.4, WL 130.2-137.8; the triangle FS 274.7-283.9 at its top edge (WL 137.8), its point FS 278.7, WL 130.1. dvids9820782 shows the same pair on the left where they project. The ink and lettering against the paint round them, sRGB (43, 59, 75) and (104, 120, 138) against (115, 136, 150)
stencils.note: the ejection-seat warnings under the cockpit on each side (plan #8: the functional stencils stay); their text as the photos read it

cockpit.unit: [FS, WL] in on the centreline: the seat's headbox from its lower front corner round; the HUD frame's foot and top; the glareshield's aft edge
cockpit.where: dvids9820808, seen through the canopy and cast onto the centreline's plane (verify/cast.py)
cockpit.note: what the simple cockpit is placed by. Its widths, the tub's floor and walls, the instrument panel and the pilot's limbs are estimated round these and the canopy's sill: no source gives them, and the detailed cockpit (step 6) replaces all of it in first person

antennas.unit: dorsal and spine: [FS, WL] corners on the centreline, the base's front and aft, the tip's aft and front; dome: [FS, WL, BL, diameter, standing proud]; comb: the stations of the posts under the nose; chin: [from FS, to FS, standing proud] of the fairing under the radome; in
antennas.where: dvids9820808 cast onto the centreline (the blades, the comb and the chin fairing); dvids9820782 sees the blades from the left on the centreline; the dome triangulated from its top and base in dvids9820808 and 9820782 (rays 81 deg apart, missing each other by 0.2-0.5 in): on the crown at FS 463.4, base WL 146.2, top 147.3, BL 0.8, about 5.4 in long in dvids9820808's profile. (Cast from dvids9820782 alone onto the skin, it had read FS 443.8, BL -12.7: that photo looks along the spine, and its sight line met the broader spine's flank 20 in short of the crown)
antennas.note: the dorsal blade antennas, the dome antenna on the spine's crown, and the small antennas under the radome. The blades' thickness and the comb posts' size are estimated

pods.unit: [FS of the front, FS of the aft end, WL, diameter] in, each pod top to bottom
pods.where: the reference airframe's right fin in dvids9820808 and dvids9820801 (BuNo 164718), each pod's aft end, top and bottom cast onto the fin's posed plane: the two agree within 0.4 in in height and 0.3-0.8 in at the ends (the fronts, tapering into the fin, from dvids9820808 alone). The diameters are the heights along the canted plane. dvids9820799 shows the left fin's inboard face carrying the same set, so each straddles the fin
pods.note: the antenna fairings on each fin's trailing edge below the tip, on the fixed fin above the rudder: the upper one (8 in below the tip) and the large one stand 1.7 and 3.2 in past the trailing edge, the middle one 1.0, the lowest ends at it. dvids8842845 (BuNo 165214) carries a different set, without the middle one. Earlier the upper pod alone was built, 645.6-658.3 at WL 204.8, 3.2 in across, from one cast onto the plane at BL 69

blade.unit: FS in; the bottom edge as [from FS, to FS, WL] in
blade.where: dvids9820808, cast onto the centreline's plane; dvids9820799, seen from ahead, puts it on the centreline within its chord
blade.note: the blade antenna under the nose ahead of the nose gear (stencilled DO NOT PAINT). Its thickness is not measured

hook.unit: [FS, WL] in, on the centreline; pivot: the centre of the pivot fitting's end cap; point: the stowed shoe's aft tip; length: pivot to tip, in; shank: in, near the pivot; fitting: in
hook.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json: hook_pivot in dvids9820808 and navy090707N7665E003, FS 649.9 +-2.3, WL 77.6 +-3.5 (dvids9820808 cast onto BL 0 alone: 647.5, 76.9); hook_point in navy090707N7665E003 alone on the centreline, FS 713.6 +-2.7, WL 96.3 +-4.0, between the nozzles. Length: 66.4 in to that point; the lowered hook's shoe cast onto BL 0 in dvids9820748 (FS 718.1, WL 59.3: 70.6 in, 15 deg down) and dvids9820749 (718.9, 74.6: 69.1 in, 2.5 deg down), whose shank also casts to the pivot (648.4, 77.5); the point is placed at their mean, 68.7 in, along the stowed direction (16.3 deg up aft). Shank depth from dvids9820808 (29 px at 0.097 in/px), width from navy090707N7665E003 (22 px at 5 px/in); the fitting's cap 5 in across in dvids9820808
hook.note: the stowed hook hangs below the aft fuselage from its pivot at the keel's aft end, its shank climbing 16 deg aft into the channel between the nacelles, its shoe tucked between the nozzles. The earlier build placed the point at FS 684 from a mark on the place the shank passes into the body's outline in a side view (about 30 in forward of the shoe) and the pivot 9 in forward: a 43 in rod. The lowering travel (62 deg) is provisional

nozzle.unit: FS in; radius in at start and exit; WL in of the axis
nozzle.where: the exit's station: overall.exhaust, 54.4 ft aft of the nose apex (nose.apex, FS 60.5); the axis's waterline: the sky check (verify/skyline.py) over the 13 photos that see the nozzles, built at WL 106, 104.5 and 103 (2026-11-02): the photos' median misses fall from 2.5 to 1.5 to 0.8 in, in flight and parked alike, and the nozzle's start then meets layout.nacelle's bottom line at FS 692 (WL 86.0) within 0.5 in, where WL 106 left it 2.5 in above; the circle fits of the exits had put their centres 1.5-3.9 in low (dvids8842845's closed right exit 3.65 +-0.5). The lower lip's WL 90.45 +-2.1 from four rear views (since out of the solve) sits 1.4 sigma above; the closed exit: dvids8842845's right exit fitted as a circle (FS 713.4 +-1.6, outer radius 10.1 +-0.35 in, 2026-11-01)
nozzle.note: the nozzles' outer flaps on the engine axes. The exit stood at FS 720 from those four photos, rear views that hold the station loosely; every in-flight photo, nozzles closed, then read the nozzles 4-8 in long (the sky check), and at the cited exhaust plane they read 0-4 in, the parked photos unchanged. The start and the start's radius are provisional (fitted to the HATP views)

petals.unit: outer flaps per nozzle; in, the exit's radius closed (military power); in, the throat's radius closed (military) and open (full reheat); in, the tailpipe's radius where the convergent flaps start; in, the convergent flaps' length; in, the divergent flaps' length; the stepped tabs: their station as a share of the outer flaps' length from the exit, and their step round as a share of a flap's width
petals.where: the count from the three photos (both nozzles of one jet end-on, 12 brackets each; a second jet's 12 trailing-edge gaps; a third's flap tabs 30 deg apart); tm101741 printed page 3 for the nozzle areas, 220 in2 at military power and 348 in2 at full reheat; tm88273 printed page 4 for the 12 primary flaps and 12 seals inside; tm100159 figures 12 and 14 for the exit, calculated R9 24.20 cm and 23.04 cm at military power (test conditions 5 and 6: M 0.9 at 24,000 ft and M 0.4 at 30,000 ft), their mean; tp3531 figure 7 (printed page 120) for the convergent section, the 0.10-scale inner nozzle's 2.640 in bore and 0.834 in flap (its throats, 1.674 and 2.105 in at 35.390 and 18.708 deg, are tm101741's areas); the stepped tabs and the divergent flaps' length read by eye off navy020214N3896H001 (an F404 out of its jet, the nozzle open) and usaf120811FON144293
petals.note: the throat's radii are the areas' circles. The closed exit's radius is the gas path's, at the divergent flaps' faces, which the build stands 1.5 in inside the outer flaps (no source gives their thickness): closing turns each flap about its hinge until that face reaches it, the outer lip then about 10.8 in from the axis, as dvids7070877 (from behind, both nozzles closed) shows it, about 10-11 in. tm100159's R9 is GE's spec deck's, the measured jet 5-10% wider (its page 8), and a running jet on the ground at intermediate holds a wider throat (264 in2, tm4538), so a closed nozzle seen low down stands a little more open. The parked photos show the nozzles open; the HARV (tm101724's jet) had its outer flaps removed. The divergent flaps' length is the eye's (no source gives it), and so are the stepped tabs: each outer flap's aft part steps round by a quarter of its width about a third of its length from the exit, so the seams between flaps make a staircase

inlet.unit: [FS, WL, BL] in; lip: its rounded front edge's highest, lowest and most outboard points and the ends of its curve at the flat inboard wall, outer side; outline: [WL, BL] along the lip's front edge from the top corner round the outside to the bottom corner; splitter: its leading edge, top to bottom
inlet.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (15 photos solved together): the lip's and splitter's points in 2 to 4 of dvids9820748, dvids9820788, dvids8678631 and dvids9820808 each (+-0.7 to 1.9 in); the outline from the three lip traces cast onto the lip's plane (they agree within 1.5 in); the splitter's leading edge from dvids9820808 and dvids8678631 together (dvids9820748 and dvids9820788 agree within 0.7 in); the wall is the lip rim's width in dvids9820748 (10-15 px, 1.0 to 1.3 in). The lip's lower and outboard points, and its bottom corner, rest on one photo each outside the two 45 degree quarter views (dvids8678631, dvids9820808): leaving that photo out moves them up to 12 in along the quarter views' line of sight, so a mistake in its mark would go unseen there; the three lip traces cast onto the lip's plane from three cameras agree within 1.5 in, which they would not if the plane were wrong Moved whole by FS -1.5 and BL +2.1 (2026-11-02), the 22-photo solve's mean offset of its six points (corners, lips, splitter top: 1.0-2.2 in forward, 1.3-3.1 in outboard, each holding with any one photo left out): the shape the 15-photo solve fitted is kept, and the points then read within 0.2-1.0 in and the lip and splitter traces within 0.06-0.52 in
inlet.note: the lip stands 40 in aft of where the model first had it (FS 365), under the LEX-wing junction, raked 3.5 in aft from top to bottom, its flat inboard side leaning inboard at the bottom; tp3478's FS 401 section (figure 4a) shows the splitter plate there but no duct yet, which agrees. The duct inside the measured lip has a hydraulic diameter of 23.6 in, tm103703's 23.34 (engine.inlet). The splitter's leading edge stands upright at FS 381, bowing 2.7 in outboard at mid-height

nacelle.unit: keel: the stations over which each nacelle's bottom follows the HATP side view's keel line (references/profiles.json, smoothed as build.py reads it), eased onto it from the lip's bottom (layout.inlet); aft: [FS, WL] knots on to the nozzles; photo: [FS, WL, uncertainty] where an in-flight photo's outline reads the bottom
nacelle.where: the HATP figure's side view keel line between FS 436 and 540 (WL 73.3 at FS 448-452, 75.8 at 500, 78.3 at 540); dvids6696790's lower outline, a sky silhouette behind the left lip, with its camera solved among 21 photos (verify/photos.py, 7.0 px): the skin steps 0.8 in below the lip's rim right behind it and falls to WL 73.6 at FS 447 cast onto BL -29 (+-1.5 in: the camera stands 7 deg above the wing plane), where an AIM-120's radome takes the outline over; navy090707N7665E003's lit strip along the right nacelle's lower side, seen from below (3.5 px), falls at the same slope over the first 25-30 in, bottoms out near FS 490-500 and rises 2-2.5 in by FS 509-528. aft: dvids9820808's lower outline behind the hook's pivot, a sky silhouette from a camera at the underside's own height (WL 78), so its waterline barely depends on the buttline it is cast onto (BL 20 here): WL 82.0 at FS 647, 82.7 at 666, 83.9 at 676, 85.2 at 685, 86.4 at 695, 87.0 at 702 (cast.py over its camera solved among 20 photos, 9.2 px); dvids8678629 and dvids9820808 read the same stretch about 2 in low against the earlier build in the sky check (verify/skyline.py). The HATP line rose to 85.0 at FS 620 and 87.5 at 640, 3-5.5 in above that outline; it is held only to FS 540, where its climb is still gentle: from FS 540 the line rises 0.21 in/in, and no smooth line joins that climb to the photo's 82.0 at FS 647 (held to FS 580, the join creased the skin 3.9 deg). Between FS 540 and 647 the build runs a monotone cubic; the photos agree in direction there (the sky check reads the lower side 2.4 in below the earlier build at FS 576-600 in dvids9820744; the top of the keel's lit side in dvids9820808 sits at WL 79 over FS 619-641)
nacelle.note: the nacelles hang about 10 in below the belly between them (the central body's bottom, WL 84). The earlier build held each nacelle's bottom at WL 87, from a symmetric section fitted to the HATP views, and rose 10 in behind the lip into it: the photos and the line both fall instead. The build keeps each nacelle's section above its centre as it was (its shoulder meets the wing's root there) and reaches below the centre down to this line. The navy photo's strip reads 2-2.5 in below the line all along, since it cannot fix its buttline (6 in of buttline there looks like 2.5 in of waterline): it agrees with the line's shape, not its level. dvids9820808's tank below the right nacelle cannot place the line (which tank it is, centreline or station 7, is not settled, and the open gear doors hang across the nacelle's lower edge), and the other solved ground photos are in shade or behind tanks. The HATP side view's keel line is held to FS 540 only: aft of it the photo's outline sits 3-5.5 in lower (2026-10-31)

speedbrake.unit: front and back: FS in of its forward (hinge) and aft edges; half: BL in of its side edges
speedbrake.where: the speedbrake's edges traced in three rear-high photos (navy090715N6106R097 from behind, navy090712N2791J126 and navy051116N8163B002 from either quarter) and triangulated a pair at a time (2026-11-03): its side edges at BL 13.9-15.8 (mean 15.2) over FS 594-652; its forward corners at FS 581-601 (mean 592) and BL 10-13; its aft end where the longest trace ends, FS 652, which may stop short of it
speedbrake.note: built as a rectangle: its forward edge's middle bulges forward and its corners jog outboard, which no pair triangulates consistently. Before (provisional): FS 545-610, 34 in wide. The spine's ridge ahead of it is narrower: its top steps out to the speedbrake's width at the forward edge (layout.spine rear)

dorsal.unit: offsets, inches aft of the canopy's aft end (layout.canopy aft), scaled by the two models' lengths (17.07 m over 16.5); depths, inches below the section's own top (every quarter inch to 6 in, then every half); widths, the half-width (BL in) at each depth, one row per offset; tops, the section's top above the canopy's aft top (in); crease, [offset, its half-width (BL in), its height in the tops' datum (in), the turn across it (deg)] every half inch
dorsal.where: the old model's outer surface with its canopy closed (every part but the pilot), cut across at each offset (every inch from 30 in ahead to 14 in behind, where its canopy's tail stands on its base), from 40 in ahead of its canopy's aft end to 90 in behind; its half-width read at each depth below the cut's top over the centreline; tops from its canopy's aft top as one vertex near the centreline gives it, about 1.5 in low, so only their differences are used; crease, the corner at the foot of its canopy's tail where it stands on the flat-topped base: on cuts every half inch, the outline's top (highest crossing at each buttline, every 0.05 in), the point where its slope over 0.4 in either side turns most, from 30 in ahead of the canopy's aft end (where it comes in from outboard at BL 15.4 and turns 35 deg) to 10 in behind (its tip, where the tail has flattened onto the base)
dorsal.note: a last resort taken at the user's decision (2026-11-04): photos measure this stretch (layout.canopy joint, layout.spine side, crown), but the user chose the old model's shape here where the two disagree. Its canopy's aft part is a narrow bubble, about 12 in either side at its foot, on a broad flat-topped base whose corner (2-3 in below the base's top, at 16-18 in out) runs on aft along the spine; behind the canopy a hood carries the bubble's lines down onto the flat top within 12 in; the corner fades by 60-90 in aft. The bubble's foot lies at about WL 150, where the photos put the glass's lower edge (glass_edge). The build takes heights from the base's flat top (the crown): below it the old model's widths at the same heights, above it squashed to our canopy's top line ahead of FS 318 (the photos' last top reading) and the old model's own height from the canopy's aft end back, where the photos' aft top stands 0.65 in lower (+-1 in); the crease at the tail's foot is laid exactly, and the glass ends on it where the photos' glass edge runs 0.3-0.7 in below it (FS 295-319)

spine.unit: FS, WL, BL in; side, [FS, WL, BL] along the spine's side seam behind the canopy; rear, [FS, WL, BL] on the spine's top between the fins: its ridge's edge, then the speedbrake's side edges
spine.where: crown: dvids9820808's top outline (near-orthographic right profile), found column by column where the sky gives way to the jet and cast onto the centreline (verify/cast.py), its antennas left out; flank: the lower ends of the spine's panel joints, each triangulated from its trace in one photo and its trace in a second (dvids9820801 with 9820808 on the right, rays 24 deg apart; dvids9820782 with 9820788 on the left, 9 deg), the two sides averaged (they agree within 1.6 in), the rays missing each other by at most 0.7 in; deck: the line where the deck behind the LEX meets the spine's wall in dvids9820788, cast onto BL 21 (onto BL 24 it moves 0.1 in); rear (2026-11-03): the spine ridge's edge (FS 577) and the speedbrake's side edges between the fins (FS 600-640), triangulated from three rear-high photos solved on their fins and pods (navy090715N6106R097 from behind, navy090712N2791J126 and navy051116N8163B002 from either quarter) a pair at a time, each point the pairs' mean with both sides together: the ridge's edge from two readings within 0.6 in; at FS 600 four readings over WL 126.1-127.7 and BL 13.9-15.6, at 620 and 640 two each, 1.6-1.9 in apart in height. A third quarter view (navy100713N2918M085) solves on six fin marks too loosely to add; side (2026-11-03): the spine's side seam behind the canopy (panel line 22) triangulated from dvids9820801 against its mirror image in dvids9820782; dvids9820788 reads the same seam 1.6 in inside where it meets the joint's foot (FS 335), which both left photos triangulate within 0.3 in (layout.canopy joint), and 1.3, 1.0, 0.7, 0.3 in inside at FS 348, 357, 366 and 384, a gap closing steadily aft, so it is left out; its first point (FS 334) is the joint's own. The shoulder narrows steadily aft, where the cited FS 357 section stood 2-3 in wider over FS 345-370. The skin is lofted smoothly from the joint to the rear fuselage and not drawn through these points: drawn through them it narrowed behind the joint and let out again, a dip then hump of 0.2-0.7 in
spine.note: the crown runs 1.8-2.9 in below the HATP side view's top line from FS 455 to 500 (the joints' upper ends, triangulated the same way, agree with it within 0.5 in); the deck stays near the LEX root's height, 5-7 in above the nacelles' tops the rear fuselage was fitted with

keel.unit: stations: FS in, where the keel leaves the body and where it ends at the hook's pivot fitting; bottom: [FS, WL] on the centreline; width: in, across its aft end, tapering to nothing at its forward end
keel.where: dvids9820808 (the right side from a camera at WL 78): a narrow part under the centreline runs forward from the hook's pivot fitting, its lit side 4.4 in tall, its bottom a sky silhouette cast onto BL 0 at WL 75.1 (FS 619) and 74.2 (FS 641), forward of which the centreline tank's tail hides it; navy090707N7665E003 (from below): a wedge under the centreline from the pivot cap (FS 651) tapering forward to a point at FS 589, about 5 in across at the cap (25 px at 5 px/in)
keel.note: the hook hangs from its aft end. Its forward end's depth is not seen: the build rises it from the bottom line to the body over FS 589-619
